To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
sulphoraphane downregulates the expression of HSPs, 70, HSF1 and HSP 90 and upregulates p21 and some apoptosis related proteins like Bax, Bad and Apaf1 in breast cancer cells.
sulphoraphane is a potential anticancer agent that can induce apoptosis by targeting HSPs and thereby altering the expressions of some apoptotic proteins.

sulphoraphane downregulates the expression of HSP70 and 90 and HSP27 and HSF1 which results in upregulation of pro-apoptotic proteins and down-regulation of anti-apoptotic proteins in breast cancer cells and induces apoptosis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of sulphoraphanes as a potential anticancer drug and also the role of HSPs in breast carcinogenesis.
the identification of a natural compound sulphoraphane which can induce apoptosis by targeting the HSPs.
the role of HSPs, HSF-1 and their modulation by sulphoraphane which may lead to apoptosis in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sulphoraphane is a potent anticancer agent which can be considered as an adjuvant to conventional therapy in breast cancer.
sulphoraphane is a potent inducer and modulator of HSPs in breast cancer cells and this effect is more profound in cells expressing wild type p53.
sulphoraphane can be used as a potential chemotherapeutic agent in the treatment of breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
sulphoraphane induces apoptosis in breast epithelial cells through modulation of HSP27, 70 and 90 and HSP transcription factor HSF1.

sulphoraphane is a potent inducer for apoptosis in breast cancer cell lines and the underlying mechanisms involve down-regulation of HSPs, HSF1, p53 independent upregulation of pro-apoptotic protein, p21, Bax, Bad and AIF followed by down-regulations of Bcl- 2 and Bid.
sulphoraphane can induce apoptosis in breast cancer through modulation of HSP70 and 90, HSF1 and p21.
The main takeaway from our work is that
sulphoraphane can be used in breast cancer therapy by targeting HSPs and their transcription factor HSF1.
HSPs can be used as a potential target in cancer therapy.
the induction of apoptosis by sulphoraphane in breast cancer cells is not only p53 independent, but also p53 independent.
